title: Ihsan: worship as if you see Him
hook: You know how to pray now. Today is about praying, and living, with your whole heart in it.

screens.text: **Welcome to Phase 3, {{convert.first_name}}.** For two months you've learned *what* to do. Now comes the part that lasts a lifetime: doing it **well**, with your heart in it.
**Ihsan (excellence).** Asked what ihsan is, the Prophet ﷺ answered: worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you can't see Him, know that He sees you [Bukhari 50].
bubbles: You met this on Day 31, in the Hadith of Jibril: Islam (what you do), **iman** (what you believe), and this third level, ihsan.

screens.prompt: Finish the Prophet's answer ﷺ: "Worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you can't see Him…"
screens.feedback: That's it [Bukhari 50]. Seeing Him is the goal; knowing He sees you is where everyone starts.

screens.text: That answer has **two steps**: a floor anyone can stand on today, and a ceiling you grow toward for life.
bubbles: **The floor:** remembering that Allah sees you. Anyone can do that today, even mid-distraction.
**The ceiling:** feeling as if you see Him. People grow toward it for a whole lifetime.
Ihsan isn't a feeling you must have every prayer. It's attention you keep bringing back.

cards.front: "If my mind wanders in prayer, I've failed at ihsan."
cards.back: No. Wandering is normal. Ihsan is noticing and coming back, again and again.
No. "He sees me" is open to you right now. That's where everyone starts.
No. It's care, not anxiety. A learner doing their honest best is doing ihsan.
No. Allah has prescribed excellence in everything [Muslim 1955]: work, school, how you treat people.

screens.situation: Marcus has a 15-minute break at work. He usually rushes Dhuhr in three minutes so he can scroll his phone for the rest. Today he's tired.

options.text: Pray first, slowly: pause until still in each position. Scroll with whatever time is left
options.feedback: Yes. Same break, different heart. Stillness in each position is part of the prayer anyway, and the phone can wait.

options.text: Rush the prayer like usual; at least it's done
options.feedback: It counts if done properly, but rushing can spoil stillness. A few extra minutes turns a task into a meeting.

options.text: Skip the break prayer and wait for a longer break later
options.feedback: Risky. If the later break falls after Dhuhr's time ends, he misses it. Pray in time, calmly.

screens.prompt: Ihsan outside the prayer looks ordinary. Which is which?

items.text: Doing the job right when no manager is checking
items.why: Yes. You do it well because He sees, not because a boss does.

items.text: Working hard only when the manager walks by
items.why: That's care for who's watching. Ihsan remembers Allah is always watching.

items.text: Finishing the essay properly, not just enough to pass
items.why: Yes. Excellence in school counts too [Muslim 1955].

items.text: Giving the customer, the patient or your little brother your full attention
items.why: Yes. Full attention to a person is ihsan in everyday clothes.

items.text: Half-listening to your little brother while you scroll
items.why: Not quite ihsan. Putting the phone down is a small act of excellence.

items.text: On a hard day, doing a smaller best
items.why: Yes. Allah asks for *your* best, not someone else's. On a hard day it's smaller, and still ihsan.

screens.prompt: Which is the "floor" of ihsan that anyone can reach today?

options.feedback: Right. That's the second step of the Prophet's answer ﷺ, and it's open to everyone, right now.
Not quite. Distraction is normal. Ihsan is bringing your attention back.
Not quite. Extras are good, but ihsan is about how you do things, not how many.

screens.prompt: Think of one prayer that felt close, when you really meant it. What helped? Then pick one everyday thing (work, chores, a class) you could do this week "as if He sees."

chips: How do I focus better in prayer?
What does "as if you see Him" really mean?
I feel nothing when I pray. Is that bad?
How is ihsan different from just being a good person?

screens.text: Pray your next prayer "as if He sees."
steps: Before you start, stop for three slow breaths
Pray with stillness in every position
screens.optional_extra: Pick one task at work, school or home today and do it as well as you can, even if nobody notices.

screens.text: Ihsan is excellence: worship as if you see Allah, and remember that He sees you, in prayer and everywhere else.
Phase 3 isn't about adding more. It's about doing what you already do with more heart.

check.prompt: How did the Prophet ﷺ describe ihsan?

options.text: Worship Allah as if you see Him; and if you can't, know He sees you
options.feedback: Right. That's from the Hadith of Jibril [Bukhari 50].
Not quite. Ihsan is worshipping as if you see Allah, knowing He sees you [Bukhari 50].

check.prompt: Your mind wanders during prayer. What does ihsan look like?

options.text: Gently bring your attention back and keep going
options.feedback: Right. Coming back, again and again, is the practice.

options.text: Start the prayer over every time
options.feedback: Not quite. A wandering mind doesn't break the prayer. Just come back.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- The Hadith of Jibril defines ihsan as worshipping Allah as if you see Him, and if you don't see Him, knowing He sees you [Bukhari 50].
- Allah has prescribed excellence (ihsan) in everything [Muslim 1955]; the hadith's own example is slaughtering an animal gently, which shows ihsan covers everyday actions.
- Regular small deeds are most beloved to Allah [Bukhari 6464]: ihsan is about quality and consistency, not volume.
- Ihsan is a lifelong journey of the heart; mainstream teachers describe it as growing through sincere obligatory worship, then voluntary acts, dhikr and good company [Revealed Path Part III; Being Muslim, Spiritual Refinement].

**Likely questions**
- *"How do I focus in prayer?"* Practical tips: pray in a quiet spot, phone away, learn the meanings of what you say (the phrase track), slow down with stillness in each position, pause before starting. Distraction doesn't invalidate the prayer.
- *"I feel nothing when I pray."* Common and not a sign of failed faith (link Days 12 and 50). Keep praying; feelings follow consistency. Offer the mentor.
- *"Is ihsan just being a good person?"* It includes good character, but its root is awareness of Allah: doing good because He sees.
- *"Do I need to pray extra prayers for ihsan?"* No. Start with the five done well. Extras (Day 57) can come gradually.

**Escalate:** persistent intrusive doubts about whether prayers count (waswasa; link Day 26, and the mentor or imam if it's distressing).

**Don't**
- Don't set ihsan as a standard that makes them feel they're failing. Emphasize "He sees you" as the reachable floor.
- Don't push extra worship; Phase 3 is about quality, not quantity.
